summary:
Weekly AI in Action call hosted by Tal Swicegood on July 16, 2026 (about 37 minutes). Attendees: Paul Feder, Jason Golden, and Daranda. Sources: the OBS screen recording (spliced from two files; missing Tal's mic) plus the complete Gemini transcript from Google Drive, which supplied both sides of the conversation and real speaker names.

Paul opened by sharing his recent Claude work: an Azure security query set up that day to validate whether RC4 encryption is in use (disable it if not), and a CMMC cost-comparison workbook comparing onboarding and ongoing costs across their current MSP, CISO, and other candidate MSPs, built by loading vendor documents into Claude. Jason said he has Claude connected to Outlook and Ramp (their corporate card platform) but is stuck at 'I connected it, now what?'. Tal clarified terminology: connections like Outlook and Ramp are tools; an agent is essentially a personality plus a standard operating procedure that uses those tools, and it can live in the cloud or on a computer waiting for work to hit its desk.

Tal then ran three demos. First, the Builders United AI voice agent ('Avery', built on VAPI in about 30 minutes, roughly 8 cents per call): Jason called it live on speaker, it handled an out-of-scope swimming-pool request gracefully, and it can create quotes and forward calls to a human. Paul noted Ring Central may offer something similar but is expensive. Second, the Higgsfield-based marketing pipeline for Whitecap: AI drafts ideas, generates 20-second mascot (Willie) videos at about $1 each, self-checks against brand rules, and a human picks winners for Facebook/TikTok/YouTube, with recruiting as the campaign goal. Third, Claude Cowork diagnosing his slow Mac live (out of RAM, killed stray processes); he advised Opus as the model for this and noted Cowork requires the desktop app, not the website.

Tal also showed the Whitecap AI resource center: merged financials across platforms, the driver work-order notes feature that surfaces unbilled bulk pickups (worth an estimated $1,000-2,000/month), and the M&A market-scan tool built for CEO Michael Schmidt with 647 ranked markets and 45-minute cited deep-dive reports; the next step is automating FOIA requests to municipalities for disposal-capacity data.

On Paul's systems roadmap: the FieldFlo partnership for takeoff bidding analytics is early-stage; the Coins data-repository agreement was just finalized (implementation draws down purchased points, abstractions must be defined in-house, and Tal will be engaged). Tal explained he bypassed FieldFlo's gated API by recording HAR files and having Claude reverse the backend requests, extracting labor hours, OT hours, and pay rates by entity into a separate database, to be crosswalked with Coins data. Paul raised replacing Salesforce with FieldFlo's CRM: they are already licensed for FieldFlo, but its dashboards are too vanilla for the executive team, so redundant licenses are the cost issue. Tal offered to recreate the executive dashboards from the extracted data and accepted Paul's invite to the same-day 1:00 PM Eastern FieldFlo dashboards call; he asked Paul to find out whether they already pay for FieldFlo API access (Pel Software is a FieldFlo integrator Paul works with weekly). Tal closed by announcing the recurring call moves to Thursdays at 3:00 PM Eastern / 2:00 PM Central, since the UK group it originally accommodated has not been attending and US turnout is better later in the day; Paul confirmed no conflicts at that time.

Automate FOIA requests to municipal agencies for disposal-capacity data in the M&A market-scan tool
Move the recurring AI in Action call to Thursdays 3:00 PM Eastern / 2:00 PM Central

Get engaged with the Coins data-repository implementation once vendor groundwork starts, then crosswalk Coins fields with the FieldFlo labor data
Validate the Azure RC4 query results once data accumulates and disable RC4 if unused
Brainstorm with Claude on concrete uses for the existing Outlook and Ramp connections
